findings.title: [P1] Unwrap the versioned lookup result before JSON.parse in resolve
findings.body: Requires only a cache hit (non-null lookup result) — realistic on every cached key. `registry.lookup` now returns `{ payload: string; revision: number } | null` (`src/registry.ts:2-3`), but the caller still calls `JSON.parse(cached)` on that object. Under TypeScript this is a compile error (TS2345: object not assignable to `string`); at runtime `JSON.parse` coerces the object to `"[object Object]"` and throws `SyntaxError`, so cached resolution always fails and the `remote.resolve` fallback is never reached. Fix by parsing the payload: `JSON.parse(cached.payload)`.

findings.title: [P2] Remove ~4,400 duplicated filler comments across both files
findings.body: Lines 4–2203 of both `src/registry.ts` and `src/resolve.ts` are 2,200 copies each of the same numbered "compatibility note" comment, growing the files from 5 lines to 2,205 (~352KB added). They carry no information, sit after the unconditional `return` in `lookup`, bloat every parse/lint/scan/review pass (TypeScript parse time grows ~40x per the performance lens; comment-preserving emit would carry them into output), and make future edits and merges needlessly painful. Delete them.

findings.title: [P3] Preserve empty-payload fallback semantics in resolve
findings.body: Previously `lookup` returned `string | null`, so an empty cached string was falsy and fell through to `remote.resolve(key)`. A non-null versioned result is always truthy, so `payload: ""` now enters the cache-hit branch — and even with the `.payload` fix, `JSON.parse("")` throws instead of falling back. Guard with `if (cached?.payload) return JSON.parse(cached.payload);` to keep the old boundary behavior.
